items.title: ‘Honkai: Star Rail’ Version 4.5 “To Roll the Stars in Astropolis” Launches 26 August
items.summary: This week, publisher HoYoverse announced that Version 4.5, dubbed "To Roll the Stars in Astropolis", will launch into their ever-popular free-to-play
items.content:
This week, publisher HoYoverse announced that Version 4.5, dubbed “To Roll the Stars in Astropolis”, will launch into their ever-popular free-to-play turn-based role-playing game title ‘Honkai: Star Rail’ on 26 August. Facing a crisis triggered by the Voracity, the Trailblazer will officially depart for Astropolis, a key Interastral Peace Corporation stronghold, to seek aid for the disaster-stricken Planarcadia. In addition, the Trailblazer will have the opportunity to embark on a special summer vacation with Robin and Aventurine. Because we all need a break from saving the world sometimes.

Also, collabs! Honkai: Star Rail has officially announced its collaboration with MOONDROP . Sparxie-themed collaboration products and various online and offline events will gradually roll out across multiple regions worldwide, with more details to be revealed soon. Later this year, Honkai: Star Rail will also launch a surprise collaboration with Zenless Zone Zero. Characters from the world of ‘ Zenless Zone Zero ‘ will join the Trailblaze on a cosmic adventure, so do stay tuned for more details (and check below for the rest of the patch!).

Following the Express Crew’s victory over Lord Ravager Asat Pramad, the Voracity makes THEIR official appearance, once again plunging Planarcadia into a fatal crisis. To find the crucial strength needed to aid Planarcadia, the Trailblazer will attempt to evade the Voracity’s obstruction and officially depart for Astropolis, the headquarters of the Interastral Peace Entertainment. There, the Trailblazer will navigate the complex hierarchy of the IPC’s upper management to secure the key power required to help Planarcadia survive this calamity.

As the crown jewel of the IPC’s business empire, Astropolis not only embodies the elegant lifestyle of Interastral Peace Corporation workers and executives, but also serves as the vacation destination of choice for countless envoys, tycoons, and officials from across the Pan-Cosmic Trade System. In the story of this Trailblaze Continuance, which takes place either shortly or a long time after the journey in Planarcadia concludes, the Trailblazer will embark on an unforgettable interstellar vacation in Astropolis alongside Robin and Aventurine.

In this update, the 5-star Wind character on the Path of Remembrance, Robin • Summeretto, will officially debut. Since Sunday left Penacony, Robin has taken over as the head of the Oak Family. This time, Robin isn’t just here to perform, but is also on a secret mission to investigate Gopher Wood’s “legacy.” However, this superstar’s stage isn’t limited to concert venues. In combat, Robin • Summeretto will also take the stage and sing alongside her little bird band, providing buffs for the team. At the same time, her teammates’ actions will accumulate Vibes for Robin • Summeretto. After she uses her Skill and her Vibes reach a certain level, her voice will bring the team to a Fever Pitch. Whenever allies attack the enemy, they will gain buffs, and the more frequently allies take action, the stronger the buffs Robin • Summeretto provides. Furthermore, when Robin • Summeretto uses her Ultimate, she can make a designated teammate immediately take action and regenerate Energy, while simultaneously increasing her own Vibes. It’s also worth noting that in this story, Robin • Summeretto will debut her brand-new single, Only by Chasing the Wind, delivering a summery burst of vitality and surprises to fans in Astropolis and across the cosmos!

In the second half of the version, the 5-star Quantum character on the Path of Elation, Aventurine • Waveflair, will make his debut. Despite kicking off a leisurely vacation in Astropolis, Aventurine continues to secretly leverage his connections and bargaining chips, vowing to verify his conjectures about the traitor among the Ten Stonehearts one by one. As a sports enthusiast and avid surfer, Aventurine • Waveflair attacks enemies in combat using a beach volleyball or by surfing the waves. Whenever he uses an ability or a teammate takes action, Aventurine • Waveflair can accumulate Punchline and Fervor. When Fervor reaches a certain number of points, he immediately triggers an extra Elation Skill. This not only attacks all enemies but also deals multiple instances of random single-target DMG. During the next Aha Instant, Aventurine • Waveflair’s Elation Skill is further enhanced. The more actions the team takes, the higher the DMG dealt by the Elation Skill.

After the version update, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Robin • Summeretto and the limited 5-star Light Cone “Rise and Sing” will be boosted. The limited 5-star character Hyacine will concurrently receive a rerun, and the 4-star Light Cone “A Little Getaway” will also be added to the first half’s Event Warps. Starting September 12, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Aventurine • Waveflair and the limited 5-star Light Cone “Summer Rides the Surf” will be boosted, and the limited 5-star character Ashveil will also receive a rerun.

In terms of version events, the racing event “Overdrive: Whirlwind Grand Prix” will officially kick off! The Trailblazer will step up as a team principal, leading their crew to become the brightest new stars on the track. Additionally, the “Minuscule Great Adventure” event will be launching simultaneously, allowing the Trailblazer to experience some fun and relaxing stage challenges. At the same time, the Divergent Universe is getting a gameplay update. The “Planar Fissure” and “Realm of the Strange” double-drop events, alongside a brand-new piece of Trailblaze Fashion, the electronic emoti standee headwear “Aw, Look Up Here,” will all be going live as well. As for the story mission experience, starting from Version 4.5, story dialogue can be sped up. Players can toggle this feature on or off at any time during story dialogue.

Honkai: Star Rail is a free-to-play gacha title available on PC via HoYoPlay , PlayStation 5 consoles, and mobile devices ( iOS , Android via Google Play / Galaxy Store ), exceeding 150 million total downloads across all platforms since its launch back in 2023.

items.title: Honkai Star Rail x ROSTIC'S collaboration launched in Russia - animated trailer unveiled
items.summary: The event will be gradually rolled out in different cities.
items.content:
0 15 August 2026, 22:37 Boris Piletskiy The event will be gradually rolled out in different cities.

The creators of Honkai Star Rail announced in August the start of a collaboration with ROSTIC'S in Russia. An animated trailer was unveiled to celebrate the launch of the event. According to the plot, Castoria and Phaenon were tasked with: "pleasing players with a delicious and exclusive combo."

Initially, the collaboration was launched in Moscow and St. Petersburg ROSTIC'S – where "Express Combos" in collaboration with Honkai: Star Rail appeared.

On August 18, the launch is expected in other Russian cities, including: Yekaterinburg, Krasnodar, Irkutsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Omsk, Rostov-on-Don, Tyumen, and Volgograd.

Players will be able to get collectible items with Honkai Star Rail characters, as well as a promo code for in-game bonuses:

Main treasures: a collectible keychain with Phaenon or Castoria in blind boxes and an in-game promo code when ordering in the mobile app or at a self-service kiosk with authorization. Источник изображения: VK community ROSTIC'S Recently, Honkai: Star Rail developers held a special stream dedicated to update 4.5 and talked about future plans. For example, miHoYo (HoYoverse) confirmed the HSR collaboration with another of its games – Zenless Zone Zero.

The Husk of Voracity is awake, and it is hungry. It takes the combined might of the Nameless, the Masked Fools and Pearl to hold the fort while the Trailblazer starts up the Astral Express to save the refugees and look for help from the IPC.

items.title: Honkai Star Rail version 4.5 livestream codes
items.summary: Make sure to redeem these codes before they expire
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Julia Lee Published Aug 14, 2026, 10:36 AM EDT Guides Make sure to redeem these codes before they expire

Image: Hoyoverse Jump Links Honkai: Star Rail 4.5 livestream codes How to redeem codes in Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail just finished up its version 4.5 livestream , showcasing what's coming up next in the new patch. These livestreams aren't just for showing off the next patch, but they also drop three codes to redeem for free Stellar Jade and other materials.

Summer break is just about over for us, but in Honkai: Star Rail , it's just getting started. Version 4.5 will bring out special summer versions of two characters from Penacony: Aventurine Waveflair and Robin Sumeretto. Aventurine will be a Quantum Nihility character and this time, Robin will be Wind Remembrance. The stream also teased an upcoming collaboration with Zenless Zone Zero in winter 2026.

Below we list the Honkai: Star Rail version 4.5 livestream codes , as well as provide handy links to redeem them instantly.

The Honkai: Star Rail reward codes from the version 4.5 livestream are:

These codes will expire on Aug. 15 at 11:59 a.m. EDT / 8:59 a.m. PDT , so use them quickly or you’ll miss out on the free loot.

You can redeem the codes in game by opening the menu and tapping on the ellipses in the top right corner. A "redemption code" option will come up that you can select.

Image: Hoyoverse via Polygon You can also redeem them online through the Honkai: Star Rail code redeem website . You'll need to select your correct server and login through the website in order to get rewards. You will also need to have a working UID for Honkai: Star Rail . If you’ve never logged into Honkai: Star Rail in any form using your Hoyoverse account, it will not work.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima is a fun creature collector with an incomprehensible story
items.summary: Honkai: Nexus Anima spins off with creature collecting auto-battling gameplay, making for a fun change of pace, though it doesn't quite fit the story.
items.content:
It’s a big deal whenever HoYoverse launches a new game. While it’s true that a new gacha game pops up almost every day, those same gacha games are almost all lifting references or mechanics wholesale from HoYoverse titles. Genshin Impact put the company on the map and shaped what modern gacha games are, and they’ve followed up that hit with Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, each one making waves and shaking up the industry just a little bit more. It’s safe to assume that HoYoverse wants that same kind of impact from their next major title, and Honkai: Nexus Anima is certainly shaping up to be a swing in a wild new direction. Unfortunately, it’s a big swing that doesn’t fully connect at this time.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a pretty unique mix of genres and gameplay hooks. While it’s built around creature collecting and will naturally draw comparisons to Pokémon, you aren’t then taking these monsters into turn-based 1v1 battles. Instead, you use them to dive into Teamfight Tactics-style auto battles between big teams of Anima – the creature name in this world.

I’ve always been curious about these sort of idle-battler games, but never met one that hooked me. Using that formula within the context of an anime gacha game, plus mixing in tons of cute collectable creatures, totally does it for me. At first, the depth of combat doesn’t feel particularly vast. There certainly isn’t a high skill ceiling to this style of battle, even as you start mixing in numerous abilities from your Eidos companions. It’s still satisfying to play, but there is a lack of mechanical difficulty at this stage which would need to ramp up to make for a truly satisfying and absorbing endgame.

Outside of battles, Honkai: Nexus Anima will be pretty familiar to you if you’ve dabbled in HoYoverse games. The tutorial section has you exploring some small interactive maps as your chosen protagonist, feeling pretty similar to the small zones of Zenless Zone Zero or Honkai: Star Rail. When you get into the meat of the game, though, you’re tossed into a pretty rich and wide map that combines the scale of a Genshin Impact region with modern buildings and whimsical fantasy meadows.

The game is beautiful, the map is beautiful, the characters you meet are beautiful…but I don’t quite know how to describe them. There isn’t a very clear genre or style to attach Honkai: Nexus Anima to – the other games in the Honkai line were always melting pots of influence that lean heavily toward sci-fi, and Genshin Impact feels similar with a further lean towards Japanese high-fantasy. Honkai: Nexus Anime is bright and bubbly, but impossible to place in the same way.

The story, meanwhile, is not bright or bubbly, but it’s certainly equally incomprehensible. HoYoverse games have an habit of repeating the same two-hit combo in their stories of giving you an amnesiac protagonist, and tossing you into a multidimensional, intergalactic story full of multiple tiers of entities and shadowy realms and world-ending threats and confusing proper nouns. Honkai: Nexus Anima lays it on as thick as usual, with all the gravitas of a grim sci-fi epic. This is a cutesy creature collector, though. The music is whimsical, and the menus are bubbly, but there’s a disconnect between the vibe the game seems to be cultivating and the vibe the story itself is doing. The dense multi-dimensional gacha stories are an acquired taste to start with, but it’s especially egregious here, and I didn’t feel an investment in or understanding of the world I’m exploring because of it.

And that’s a shame, because it really is so much fun to explore this world. Each Anima you bond with can be summoned outside of battles to wander around with you and bust out their unique abilities. One type can smash through walls, while another can become a hilarious improvised trampoline for you to bounce off. I was pretty addicted to the gameplay loop I found myself in, where I’d spend time exploring the world to find new Anima, then I’d dive into battles to see which ones fit together best in a team. And then, once I found a team I liked, I could set out to keep training and uncapping my favourite Anima to make them as strong as possible.

It’s so much fun to play Honkai: Nexus Anima and it’s take on the creature collecting genre, but from the closed beta test, that gets lost in the bland world and incomprehensible story. Being invested in the characters and the story is my biggest reason for picking up a gacha game, and without that, I already have one foot out the door with Honkai: Nexus Anima. I’m hopeful that, as we head towards the full release, HoYoverse can massage these problems and reel me back in.

items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.
